Theme

Nature & food

brushwood noun

cut or fallen twigs

also twigs, sticks, faggot, kindling (twigs), prunings, dead wood

classical

Cic. Sen. 52 (Lewis & Short)
Col. 4.24.7 (Lewis & Short)
Varr. RR 1.31.2 (Lewis & Short)

sarmenta, sarmentōrum n. pl.

noun, second declension, plural

twigs, light branches, brushwood; vine prunings

From sarpō, prune. The singular is rare.

Other words

  • rāmālia, rāmālium n. pl. — twigs, sticks, dry branches

    noun, third declension, plural · also used · classical · Ov. Met. 8.644 (Lewis & Short); Sen. Ep. 90.10 (Lewis & Short); Tac. Ann. 13.58 (Lewis & Short)

    From rāmus.

Examples

  • sarmenta et vallōs prīmus sub tēcta refertō

    be the first to carry the prunings and the stakes back under coverVerg. G. 2.409

  • multifidāsque facēs rāmāliaque ārida tēctō dētulit

    she brought down from the roof split kindling and dry twigsOv. Met. 8.644–645

See also twig, branch, fuel, undergrowth, prune.

SourcesLewis & Short: sarmentum · Lewis & Short: ramale

Vergil, Georgica 2.409. Ovid, Metamorphoses 8.644–645.
